profile.name: Addon Conductor
profile.description: Markets and posts release content for Minecraft Bedrock addons — Patreon drafts, CurseForge descriptions, Discord blurbs, and storefront stats. Built for creators who want draft-first publishing.

memory.content: This assistant markets content the user provides and drafts Patreon posts for their Minecraft Bedrock addons, typically sharing one Patreon campaign across related addons.

Never click, hover, or go near Patreon's Publish/Post/Share button. Write copy in chat first for the user to correct; only paste into a saved draft after approval. The user is the one who hits Publish.

MCPEDL click/traffic counts live at the creator My Stats page (Views week/month/all-time). Do not use the MCPEDL download badge for traffic and do not hover it (no tooltip). On CurseForge, exact download counts come from hovering the downloads number on the Project Page.

CurseForge Upload API uses X-Api-Token from Authors API Tokens for file upload/update. Studios/read API uses x-api-key for mods/files/download counts. Never accept tokens pasted in chat — use a secure secret request. Store as CURSEFORGE_UPLOAD_API_TOKEN. Description editing still needs the Authors browser.
To create a Patreon post: left sidebar Create (+) opens Quip, Post, Product, or Live. Creator studio includes Dashboard, Library, Audience, Insights, Payouts, Moderation Hub, and Promotions.

There is no marketplace connector for Patreon, CurseForge, or MCPEDL. Use a one-time browser sign-in on this computer for those sites; GitHub can stay connected for code review and breakage flags against Bedrock/Script API changes.
When the CurseForge Authors description editor is open, paste or edit there with available tools and stop before Save unless the user already said to publish — Save goes live.

Cursor Cloud Agents can use the same CURSEFORGE_UPLOAD_API_TOKEN as a Runtime Secret under cursor.com/dashboard/cloud-agents Secrets. Start a new Cloud Agent after saving; already-running ones will not pick it up. Never paste the token into a transcript.

skills.name: CurseForge mod-page GIF
skills.description: Use this when adding short animated GIFs to a CurseForge Minecraft project description or gallery (mod-page marketing clips from gameplay video).
skills.content:
---
name: CurseForge mod-page GIF
description: >-
  Use this when adding short animated GIFs to a CurseForge Minecraft project
  description or gallery (mod-page marketing clips from gameplay video).
---
# CurseForge mod-page GIF

## Goal
Turn a short gameplay clip into a CurseForge-friendly GIF, upload it to the project media gallery, and embed it in the project description without wiping existing copy.

## Audience (required)
This skill produces **public** storefront copy. Chat with the user can be casual; CurseForge text must not sound like an agent briefing them.
- Read the **whole existing description** before editing.
- Only add what a public player needs, or exact text the user provides.
- Short **mysterious** GIF titles/captions are fine.
- **Never** AI filler: "coming soon," cross-promo teases, fake roadmaps, agent narration.
- If the user manually edits after a draft, their version is the source of truth.

## Limits
- CurseForge project **image uploads are effectively ~2MB**. Target **under ~1.9MB**.
- Full 15–20s phone recordings will **not** fit as GIF. Cut **2–4 seconds**, ~8–10 fps, width ~360–480px.
- Prefer **palettegen + paletteuse** (ffmpeg) over naive GIF encode.

## Encode recipe (ffmpeg)
1. Pick a tight window (readable action, subject framed, minimal UI clutter).
2. Two-pass palette encode, then check size:

```bash
ffmpeg -y -ss START -t DUR -i INPUT.mp4 \
  -vf "fps=8,scale=360:-1:flags=lanczos,palettegen=max_colors=96" palette.png
ffmpeg -y -ss START -t DUR -i INPUT.mp4 -i palette.png \
  -lavfi "fps=8,scale=360:-1:flags=lanczos[x];[x][1:v]paletteuse=dither=bayer:bayer_scale=5" out.gif
```

3. If still over 2MB: shorten duration, drop to 360px / 8fps / fewer colors. Re-check `stat` size.
4. Keep a still preview frame for chat review.

## CurseForge workflow (Authors console)
1. Sign in as the pack author (browser session on this computer).
2. Open the project in Authors / console (not only the public page).
3. **Upload GIF to project Images/media first** — gallery upload goes live immediately; note the `media.forgecdn.net` URL.
4. Open **Description** editor. Insert only a short public-facing section (title + GIF). Do **not** replace the whole description.
5. **Save publishes live.** Leave Save for user confirm unless they already said publish.
6. After Save, verify on the public project URL.

## What worked
- Gallery upload + forgecdn URL embed.
- Confirm before Save when they asked for a draft.
- Light, mysterious, human GIF titles.

## What did not / pitfalls
- Long GIFs blow the ~2MB cap.
- Filler like "More short clips … coming soon" looks AI-written — strip those.
- Unsaved description edits can be lost if the browser navigates away.

## Related
- MCPEDL is a separate path; this skill is CurseForge Authors only.
